title: Finite generation of ideals lifted in an adically complete ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $J,K\subseteq A$ ideals. Suppose $A$ is $J$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] and $\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring] is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Then $K$ is finitely generated.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, lines 23022–23063), steps 3–6 (approximation, iteration and convergence)

proof.text: Obtain finitely many h_i in K with degrees d_i and one-step approximation for K ∩ J^n from the initial-form approximation theorem.
For x in K recursively subtract one-step approximations. Let r_n belong to K ∩ J^n and c_i(n) belong to J^(n-d_i). Put s_i(N)=sum_{n<N} c_i(n). Induction gives x-sum_i s_i(N) h_i=r_N.

Put D=max_i d_i, with D=0 for an empty family. Induct on N≥M to show s_i(N)-s_i(M) lies in J^k whenever M≥k+d_i. Thus k↦s_i(k+D) is an adic Cauchy sequence. Precompleteness supplies L_i with s_i(k+D)-L_i in J^k for every k.

The telescoping remainder r_(k+D) lies in J^k; so does sum_i (s_i(k+D)-L_i)h_i. Therefore x-sum_i L_i h_i lies in J^k for every k. Separatedness gives x=sum_i L_i h_i. Since all h_i lie in K, their finite range spans exactly K.
